claim: An investor forecasting dividend yield, earnings growth, and P/E growth separately (sum-of-the-parts) rather than forecasting total market return directly would have achieved a certainty-equivalent gain of up to 2.3% per year and a 77% higher Sharpe ratio than a historical-mean benchmark.
stance_target: decomposed, durability-tagged return forecasting outperforms blended single-multiple approaches
scope_conditions: US aggregate market, real-time out-of-sample simulation, 1927-2007
quoted_support: An investor who timed the market with our approach would have had a certainty equivalent gain of as much as 2.3% per year and a Sharpe ratio 77% higher relative to the historical mean.
